A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AC-LoRA system. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original memorization, retrieval, question-answering, knowledge-combination, multimodal, and latency experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds empirical evaluations of hinting and retrieval-based selection versus mixing all LoRAs.

M1.justification: Permission-specific adapters, permission-filtered retrieval, similarity-weighted mixing, and hinting remain unchanged. The new document-score averaging explanation clarifies an existing mechanism; discussion of disabling sensitive hints does not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same confidential/quantum-computing papers, RepLiQA and CS-COMBI, FlanV2, WikiArt, and MMSci coverage. The added hinting and all-LoRA analyses reuse existing tasks and datasets with different permission or adapter controls.

E2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds mixing all LoRAs as a comparator on RepLiQA and FlanV2. SMEAR, AdapterSoup, and LoRAHub disappear from the main summary table but remain in the corresponding detailed FlanV2 comparison in Table C.1, so those methods were not removed from the evaluation.

E3.justification: The new hinting evaluation masks the expected topic adapter, then evaluates with all permissions when a hint was produced. The new all-LoRA comparison adds another adapter-selection control. Existing splits, training budgets, model configurations, and grading metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct component evaluations absent from v1: Appendix C.2.1 tests whether granting access following a hint improves answers, and C.3 tests the benefit of selecting relevant adapters instead of mixing all adapters. These substantially extend component validation beyond the retained retrieval-parameter and LoRA-rank analyses.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and C.1 add explicit 95% confidence intervals throughout the AC-LoRA FlanV2 results, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting for the principal benchmark comparison. v1 already contained shaded bands in plots. v2 does not explain interval construction or establish additional repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Existing FlanV2 point estimates and principal plotted findings remain unchanged. New results include hinting grade curves in Figure C.6 and comparisons against mixing all LoRAs: RepLiQA gains 0.066 with a 95% interval of (-0.00748, 0.138), while Table C.3 reports FlanV2 gains including 34.64 for ROUGE-1 and 9.76 for translation. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The permission-set definitions, similarity-weighted mixing equations, threat assumptions, and Appendix A memorization calculations remain unchanged. No new formal theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: access-control-aware serving, training-free LoRA mixing, competitive performance, knowledge combination, and multimodal applicability. The added experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 extends discussion of overlapping knowledge groups, GPU-memory bottlenecks, sensitive-hint suppression, and possible disruption of model alignment or content filters. Appendix C.3 adds interpretations of the all-LoRA comparison. The principal conclusions and five existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a project code-repository link and declares the implementation open source. v2 also documents approximate memory requirements, clarifies document-score aggregation, and defines the existing IID/OOD settings in Table 2. The detailed hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and prompts are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the original RAG paper, Privacy-aware RAG, GPT vs RETRO, and Llama Guard. These extend discussion of retrieval privacy, fine-tuning versus retrieval, and alignment safeguards; the central positioning against existing LoRA-mixing methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes distributed wording and grammar edits, updates affiliations and the conference header, and adds a NeurIPS checklist, appendix contents, and subsections for the new analyses. The main narrative and existing appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the hinting plot and all-LoRA comparison table, expands table columns to accommodate confidence intervals, simplifies Table 2, and adds explanatory footnotes. Existing diagrams, plots, and generated-image examples are retained with layout shifts and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new component evaluations, confidence intervals in Tables 2 and C.1, code-access information, and deployment/security discussion improve evidential support and transparency. The gains are limited by unspecified uncertainty-estimation procedures and a RepLiQA all-LoRA comparison whose interval includes zero. The core method, principal results, and broader validation limitations remain unchanged.
